exceptions: A qualifying direct international arrival to Jeju, without transit through another part of Korea, may use the separate Jeju visa-free scheme. The nationality exclusions and itinerary conditions must be met.
The temporary K-ETA waiver does not apply to Indonesian nationality.

From 28 May through 31 December 2026, Indonesian tour groups of at least 3 people recruited by a designated Indonesian travel agency may qualify for visa-free travel throughout Korea for up to 15 days. The linked Korean agency must submit the group list for Ministry of Justice pre-screening and approval. Approved travelers must hold valid passports and enter and leave together on the same flight or vessel. This scheme does not grant visa-free entry to independent tourists.
fields.entry_requirements: An ordinary Indonesian tourist must obtain the appropriate visa before travel unless a specific visa-free entry scheme applies.

fields.passport_validity: Valid at entry and throughout the authorised stay. Korean immigration law publishes no minimum remaining validity for entry. Separately, the Korean Embassy in Jakarta accepts the visa application only if the passport has at least 6 months of validity left on the submission date (rule in force since 3 November 2014, with a discretionary exception for urgent humanitarian entry).

disposition.note: Official MOFA rule: If your country is not listed, you must apply for a visa to enter Korea. The complete current K-ETA nationality list excludes Indonesia. Ordinary independent tourism requires a visa; separate approved-group (28 May–31 December 2026), Jeju and transit exceptions require their own conditions.
